security_audit.summary: AI adjudication found many static hits were documentation, generated reports, tests, CSS, schemas, or scanner artifacts rather than active threats. Confirmed residual risks are concentrated in local command execution, package and install filesystem mutation, archive handling, outbound provider or GitHub calls, runtime credential environment access, and two unscanned artifacts.

remediation.issue: Local command execution surfaces are included in scripts and Makefile targets.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running command, adaptation, CI, output execution, or sync workflows, and keep allowlists narrow.

remediation.issue: Provider, GitHub, and update workflows can perform outbound network requests and read credential environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Document every outbound endpoint, keep HTTPS and host allowlists enforced, and never log or persist API key values.

remediation.issue: Packaging and install simulation mutate local directories and handle zip archives.
remediation.suggestion: Keep path traversal checks, protected install prefixes, dry-run modes, and archive entry validation mandatory for all package workflows.

remediation.issue: Generated reports and a binary preview artifact include scanner blind spots or very large content.
remediation.suggestion: Manually review unscanned artifacts before marketplace publication and consider excluding generated reports from the published package.

content.value_statement: Teams need repeatable agent skills that are documented, tested, and packaged. This skill guides creation, evaluation, governance, and release evidence across Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Turns repeated workflows, prompts, transcripts, and notes into structured skill packages.
Routes deeper guidance through references while keeping SKILL.md compact.
Generates evaluation, packaging, registry, trust, and review evidence through local scripts.
Supports OpenAI, Claude, generic, and VS Code packaging targets through cross-packaging tools.
Builds static overview, Review Studio, Skill Atlas, and world-class evidence reports.
Defines governance gates for production, team, library, and release-critical skills.
limitations: Many capabilities require running local Python scripts and Makefile targets.
Provider-backed evaluation requires user-supplied API credentials and explicit network access.
World-class readiness still depends on external evidence and human review packets.
Generated reports and package artifacts can be large and may require manual review.

use_cases.title: Package a Team Workflow
use_cases.description: Convert a repeated internal workflow into a reusable skill with clear boundaries, outputs, and release checks.

use_cases.title: Audit a Skill Release
use_cases.description: Run trust, packaging, registry, install, and review evidence before sharing a skill with a wider team.

use_cases.title: Improve Skill Quality
use_cases.description: Use evaluations, overview reports, and Review Studio evidence to find weak routing, output, or governance areas.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Skill Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner authoring from a repeated task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this repeated workflow into a lean skill draft. Identify the job, inputs, output contract, exclusions, and the smallest useful file structure.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an Existing Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve a current SKILL.md and supporting files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this skill package for trigger clarity, output boundaries, missing references, and unnecessary complexity. Suggest focused edits and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Release Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare the release evidence plan for this skill. Include trust, packaging, install simulation, registry, output evaluation, and review gates.

prompt_templates.title: Adjudicate Readiness Gaps
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before marketplace or internal publication.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the generated reports and identify readiness gaps. Separate local evidence, human-required evidence, external-required evidence, and overclaim risks.

output_examples.input: A support escalation workflow repeated by an operations team.
output_examples.output: A concise skill plan with trigger text, required inputs, response contract, exclusions, evaluation cases, and release gates.

output_examples.input: A skill package with generated trust and Review Studio reports.
output_examples.output: A readiness summary that lists passed gates, blocked evidence, manual review needs, and the next smallest verification step.

output_examples.input: A messy set of prompts, notes, and examples for a developer workflow.
output_examples.output: A normalized package structure with SKILL.md, references, scripts, evals, and clear boundaries for future maintenance.

best_practices: Keep SKILL.md lean and move durable method detail into references or scripts.
Run the focused verifier first, then run make ci-test before release evidence sign-off.
Treat planned, local, human, and external evidence as separate readiness states.
anti_patterns: Do not create a skill for one-off requests that have no repeated workflow.
Do not hand-edit generated reports when a generator exists.
Do not claim world-class readiness from templates, plans, or missing external evidence.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create reusable AI agent skills with structure, evaluations, packaging, governance, and release evidence.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The package declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it require running scripts?
faq.answer: Many verification, packaging, report, and install simulation workflows require local Python or Makefile commands.

faq.question: Does provider evaluation need credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. Provider-backed output evaluation requires a user-supplied API key in the local environment.

faq.question: Is it only for new skills?
faq.answer: No. It can also refactor, evaluate, package, and govern existing skill packages.

faq.question: What should reviewers check before publishing?
faq.answer: Review subprocess use, network calls, credential environment access, local install behavior, archive handling, and generated artifacts.
